title: Deletion Dry-Run Simulator and Verifiable Drill Runbook
creator: Ethan Rivera
description:
Problem: Customers and internal auditors need confidence that our automated deletion and RTBF processes actually remove data by policy across regions, storage backends, and downstream caches. Current purge automation covers execution and attestation generation, but lacks a safe, repeatable way to rehearse deletions, measure false-negatives/positives, and produce a tamper-evident drill report for regulators and security reviews.

Goal: Build a 'dry-run simulator' that executes retention/deletion policies against a non-production snapshot (metadata-only or synthetic dataset) and produces a verifiable drill report. Deliver a runbook and UI to schedule periodic drills (customer-initiated or Redwood-run), compare expected-to-actual deletion outcomes, and generate an auditable, cryptographically-signed drill artifact suitable for compliance audits and third-party attestation.

Scope:
- Simulator service that replays retention rules across tenant scopes and geozones using a read-only copy of metadata and synthetic payload markers.
- Drill orchestration: schedule, run, retry, and cancel with tenant-scoped configs and RBAC controls.
- Evidence pack: expected-deletes vs simulated-deletes, diff summary, per-object hash chain, signed report + provenance metadata for upload to customer portal.
- UI/Console workflow to run drills, view summary, and download signed artifacts; API to trigger programmatically.
- Operator safety guardrails: rate limits, sandboxed executions, explicit consent for any simulated mutations, and no mutations of production storage.

Out of scope for this ticket: running drills that perform real irreversible deletes in production, integration with every existing downstream consumer (will validate via sampling and interfaces).
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run simulator can execute retention policies for a given tenant and geozone using a non-destructive metadata snapshot within a simulated execution environment
Simulator produces a drill report containing: expected deletions, simulated deletions, diffs, per-item SHA256 hashes, and a tamper-evident signature (service signing key)
Console exposes a 'Run Drill' workflow with scheduling, tenant scope selection, and preflight checks; API endpoint exists to trigger and fetch drill reports
Operator and customer roles are enforced (RBAC) for drill creation and artifact download; audit log entries created for each drill run
Automated checks detect >1% discrepancy between expected and simulated deletes and open a routing alert to the compliance oncall with a reproducible repro and suggested triage steps
Runbook documenting step-by-step drill execution, interpretation of results, and remediation actions is published to Confluence and linked from the report UI
tasks: Design simulator execution model (metadata snapshot format, synthetic marker injection, sampling strategy) - (PM/Eng sync)
Prototype sandbox runner service (k8s job + read-only data mounts) with cost/latency guardrails
Implement drill orchestration API: POST /drills, GET /drills/:id, GET /drills/:id/report
Build evidence pack generator: expected vs simulated CSVs, JSON diffs, per-item hash chain, and signature metadata
Console UX: Drill creation modal, progress stream, result summary, and artifact download link
RBAC changes: new permissions 'drill:create', 'drill:view', 'drill:download' and mapping to roles
Alerting playbook: threshold rules, oncall routing, and auto-created investigation ticket template
Write Confluence runbook and customer-facing guide for scheduling compliance drills
Security review and key-management integration for signing artifacts (KMS/HSM)
risks: Simulator incorrectly models production state and produces false assurance (mitigation: conservative sampling, explicit caveats in reports)
Signing key compromise undermines trust in drill artifacts (mitigation: use KMS/HSM, rotate keys, and store revocation metadata)
Operational cost if drills run too frequently or against large metadata sets (mitigation: quotas, size caps, sampling)
Legal/regulatory concerns if synthetic markers are considered test data that crosses residency boundaries (mitigation: per-geozone config and tenant consent flows)
notes: Design decision (2026-02-18): prefer metadata-only snapshots and deterministic synthetic markers over copying full payloads to avoid PII exposure in sandboxes
Suggested sampling approach: stratified sampling by object age, storage tier, and replication factor to increase coverage of edge cases
Evidence format proposal: a compressed bundle containing index.json (metadata), expected.csv, simulated.csv, diffs.json, hashes.txt, signature.sig, and provenance.md
Prototype spike (ENG) is planned for 2026-02-22; initial results will determine iteration speed
Linked artifacts: Confluence draft (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Drill+Runbook+Draft), Spike PR (github.com/redwood-inference/purge-sim-proto/pull/12)
